conceptual assets.information: The XLEN-bit result of the conditional operation, carrying rs1_i when the command is valid and the condition is true, and zero otherwise; downstream execution depends on this returned value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An integrator may treat the operand and computed result as private data, and res_o directly exposes rs1_i at line 54. The result can be changed by the valid and condition decisions that select rs1_i or zero at lines 53-57. Those same decisions can withhold the useful result by assigning zero at lines 55-56, preventing the required operation result from being delivered.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who influences the operands or command-control inputs could observe res_o or force the unit to return zero or an incorrect result instead of the intended rs1_i value.

conceptual assets.information: The rs2_i operand value used to determine whether the conditional operation passes rs1_i; the raw operand is only tested internally and is not returned as a whole.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: An integrator may treat rs2_i as private operand data, and the choice between rs1_i and zero at lines 53-56 exposes information about whether the operand satisfies the tested condition at line 62. Changing rs2_i changes rs2_zero and the condition at lines 62-63, thereby changing the result decision. An altered operand can make the unit suppress the useful result and output zero at lines 55-56.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter or observe the condition operand so that the predicate is changed or inferred from whether res_o returns rs1_i or zero.

conceptual assets.information: The decision indicating whether the selected comparison condition is satisfied, computed from rs2_i and ctrl_i.ir_funct3(1); it controls whether the result path passes rs1_i or returns zero.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The predicate can be sensitive because res_o reveals its effect by selecting rs1_i or zero at lines 53-56. The decision is produced by the comparison and XNOR logic at lines 62-63 and directly controls the result assignment at line 53. A false or blocked decision withholds the operation result and causes zero to be returned at lines 55-56.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could influence rs2_i or the condition-selecting control bit to force the decision true or false, corrupting or suppressing the conditional result.

conceptual assets.information: The status indicating that the control input encodes this conditional operation, reported to the surrounding processor through valid_o; it is decoded from instruction-operation selector fields rather than stored.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The status is generated by the operation-valid decode at lines 41-43 and drives valid_o at line 66, so an altered decode or control value can report a valid operation when none is present or suppress a valid one. If valid_o is withheld or forced low, the surrounding processor can fail to recognize and use the operation result, as shown by the valid status output at line 66.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker who influences the control fields could falsely assert or suppress valid_o, causing the surrounding processor to accept an invalid operation or lose a valid one.

considered, not kept.reason: Operation Selectors (a) makes opcode, function and validity fields that only identify the operation part of the operation rather than a separate conceptual asset.
The clock and reset only time or reset res_o, so the Clocks and resets rule bars them as conceptual assets.
